newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Brokers cut NKF estimates on profit shock.
newsitem.headline: Brokers cut NKF estimates on profit shock.

text.p: Brokers said on Tuesday they were slashing their profit forecasts, and many of them were downgrading their recommendations, for Dutch cable maker NKF Holding in the wake of its surprise profit warning on Monday.
Shares in NKF plunged 24 percent on Monday after it said 1997 profits were expected to be substantially lower than those of 1996 as a result of a fall in prices in Germany.
The shares were unchanged at 56.00 guilders at 1430 GMT.
Analysts said they were cutting earnings per share (EPS) forecasts for 1997 to between 3.75 and 4.95 guilders, compared with between 6.81 and 7.94 before the profit warning.
Forecasts for 1998 EPS were lowered to between 4.70 and 5.70 guilders, down from 7.40 and 9.05 previously.
Actual profits in 1996 were 44.1 million guilders, or 6.81 guilders per share.
"Obviously we were completely caught off guard," said Rabo Securities analyst Steef Bergakker, who put out a strong buy recommendation on the company the previous week.
He has now cut his recommendation to a hold.
"We think the fundamental value is considerably above current value but Dutch investors will need six to 12 months to recover from a shock like this," he added.

Analysts said the problem for NKF was in the power cables market in Germany, where large electricity utilities used their bargaining power to demand price cuts of 25 percent for 1997 compared with an expected five to 10 percent decline.
F van Lanschot Bankiers analyst Clara van der Elst also downgraded her recommendation to underperformance, equivalent to a sell, from outperformance, or a buy.
"This came as complete surprise for the company as well," she said.
BZW analyst Manus Fleskens noted that half the NKF analysts recently polled had regarded the company as a buy.
"That's hard to maintain," said Fleskens, adding that his forecast had been the lowest and he was keeping his sell advice.
Michael Molenaar of Theodoor Gilissen said NKF was small but active in markets suffering overcapacity and low growth and it was selling to customers that could dictate prices.
He said it also had little scope to keep cutting costs to compensate for price reductions.
"They're already very lean and mean," he said.
Bob Kommers of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett also cut his NKF profit estimates but maintained his hold recommendation, saying the price correction was in line with the earnings adjustments.
Kommers said he was also cutting his profit forecasts for other Dutch cable companies Draka and Twentsche Kabel .
He cut Draka's EPS for 1997 by 25 cents to 5.30 guilders and for 1998 by 40 cents to 5.75.
For Twentsche Kabel, he lowered EPS by 15 cents to 7.55 guilders for 1997, by 25 cents to 8.15 in 1998 and by 35 cents to 8.75 in 1999.
Suez Nederland earlier lowered its recommendation on NKF to a sell from a hold.
-- Garry West, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
